'''''Crataegus punctata''''' is a species of [[Crataegus|hawthorn]] known by the common names '''dotted hawthorn'''<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |accessdate=2014-10-17 }}</ref><ref>{{PLANTS|id=CRPU|taxon=Crataegus punctata|accessdate=17 January 2016}}</ref> or '''white haw''' that is native to most of the eastern United States and eastern Canada. While some sources claim it is the state flower of [[Missouri]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.50states.com/flower/missouri.htm|title=Missouri State Flower|work=50states.com|access-date=12 September 2015}}</ref> the actual legislation does not identify an exact species.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.moga.mo.gov/statutes/C000-099/0100000030.HTM|title=Section 10-030 State floral emblem.|work=mo.gov|access-date=12 September 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131022010815/http://www.moga.mo.gov/statutes/C000-099/0100000030.HTM|archive-date=22 October 2013}}</ref> Furthermore, the Missouri Department of Conservation asserts the ''[[Crataegus mollis]]'' was specifically designated as the state flower.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://mdc.mo.gov/discover-nature/field-guide/hawthorns|title=Hawthorns|author=anonymous|work=mo.gov|access-date=12 September 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150915054235/http://mdc.mo.gov/discover-nature/field-guide/hawthorns|archive-date=15 September 2015}}</ref>

== Description ==
Although many North American hawthorns are [[polyploid]] and reproduce by [[apomixis]], this species is apparently diploid and sexual, at least throughout Ontario, Canada.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Talent |first1=N. |last2=Dickinson |first2=T.A. |year=2005 |title=Polyploidy in ''Crataegus'' and ''Mespilus'' (Rosaceae, Maloideae): evolutionary inferences from flow cytometry of nuclear DNA amounts |journal=Canadian Journal of Botany |volume=83 |issue=10 |pages=1268–1304 |doi=10.1139/b05-088 }}</ref> The name '''white haw''' refers to its distinctive pale (grey) bark, which is particularly noticeable in the winter landscape. The plant is a bush or small tree to about 7 meters in height and very thorny, particularly on the trunk. The flower has three to five styles and approximately 20 stamens, and the fruit is a [[pome]]-type [[Pyrena|polypyrenous]] [[drupe]] which contains three to five pits. Anther colour varies from deep purple through red to pink to white, and the mature fruit colour can be deep burgundy, scarlet, yellow, or yellow with a red cheek.
